title: late-night-kernel-surgery-notes-noah
content:
Context: did a late-night dive after pager to isolate a 99p token latency tail that popped up in canary. Quick notes — messy, for handoff and followups.

What I observed:
- Spike in 99p token latency on model-x-small-v2 during steady qps ~2200/s at ~02:10 UTC.
- Traces show long stalls inside kvcache::read() and periodic GC-ish pauses in kernel thread: 'evict_scan' getting stuck ~18-45ms.
- Effect most visible for sequences >512, not uniform across replicas.

Quick repro (local-ish):
- Start micro-batch harness with model-x-small-v2, concurrent 128 clients, request length 640, prefix caching enabled.
- Use: ./scripts/loadtest --concurrency 128 --seq-len 640 --batch-policy continuous --warmup 60s
- Repro of 99p tail seen after ~120s in local run (flaky but repeatable).

Hypotheses:
1) Eviction scan lock contention: large-kv scans block writers and stall token emission.
2) Batch scheduling edge-case: when many sequences >512, kernel picks bad slot and causes backpressure + cache thrash.
3) Mis-tuned GC threshold after recent quantization patch — triggers synchronous compaction.

Quick experiments I ran:
- Disabled prefix caching on canary -> tail reduced but overall throughput dropped 7%. (tradeoff: latency vs cost)
- Increased eviction-window from 512->1024 in runtime config -> lowered stalls in one replica, other replica still noisy.
- Rebuilt with debug-locks: inserted lightweight timing around eviction loop -> confirms long pauses correlate with threads waiting on eviction_mutex.

Immediate mitigation (short-lived):
- Roll forward: pinned canary to model-x-small-v1 (previous known-good) and scaled down canary fraction to 5% until next deploy.
- On hosts: add node-level flag evict_scan_sleep_ms=1 to spread out scan work.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Push minimal patch to make eviction loop yield every N iterations (PR draft in my fork). Linked PR placeholder.
- [ ] Add micro-bench that simulates mixed seq lengths (256/512/1024) and record eviction lock wait histograms.
- [ ] Investigate why only some replicas affected — compare kernel build flags and runtime config (quantization flags / NUMA affinity).
- [ ] Add a temporary metric: eviction_mutex_wait_ms and expose in prom for 24h.
- [ ] Follow up with SRE tomorrow 09:30 PT to discuss gradual rollout plan.

Notes for handoff:
- If you pick this up: start by running the repro with the --trace-evict flag I added; it prints micro-timestamps to /tmp/evict-trace.log.
- Logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/evict-trace-*.log on canary hosts.
- Safe rollback plan: revert to model-x-small-v1, reduce canary to 0%, restart gateway route.

Random scribbles / hunches:
- Possible interaction with kernel prefetcher when seq >512 causing cacheline churn.
- Might be exacerbated by recent kernel-level epoll tweak (PR#4702) — check commits between 4690-4715.

Hand-off comment to Sofia/Ethan: I left the local debug branch under noah/evict-yield; it's ugly but has the timing scaffolding you need. If you can't repro, look at canary host rtr-03 (noisy) vs rtr-06 (quiet) and dump /proc/cmdline, kernel build id.

Timestamped log excerpt (from rtr-03 02:11:08):
  evict: start loop iter=0 t=0.000
  evict: had to wait on mutex for 24ms
  kvcache: read stall 28ms token-emit-block

If I get time tonight: try a version that disables synchronous compaction path entirely and run against staging. Ok that's it — low-fidelity notes. Will tidy into a small bug doc tomorrow and open proper ticket.
